newsitem.title: UK: Rains likely to hamper Europe beet harvest - Licht.
newsitem.headline: Rains likely to hamper Europe beet harvest - Licht.

text.p: Heavy rains over Europe's beet areas may hamper harvesting and increase the threat of frost damage, statistician F.O. Licht said on Wednesday.
Rains had been two to four times what was normal for September, and more were forecast, Licht said in its daily report.
"Additional rains are expected which will make harvesting extremely difficult," the report said.
"Moreover, the later the harvest, the greater the danger of an early frost, which could lead to noticeable losses."
While the very heavy rains in Europe's eastern half had finally ended, September rainfall for the area to date was still 150 to 350 percent of normal levels, Licht said.
"The rains not only affected sugar content, but also hampered harvesting operations," it said.
But while the former Soviet Union had suffered heavy rains in the week ending September 24, light rains had been seen in the southern half of Europe.
Northern areas, including most of Britain, Germany and Poland, had been mostly dry.
